items.title: U-turn ends in death of undocumented foreigner in Kluang
items.summary: Deputy district police chief Superintendent Nik Mohd Azmi Husin said the accident was believed to have occurred when the Hyundai, travelling from Simpang Renggam, made a U-turn and entered the path of a Perodua Axia travelling from Taman Sri Bayu towards Simpang Renggam. The Axia driver, identified as Muhammad Khairul Azwan, 28, was unable to avoid the Hyundai and crashed into its front passenger-side. The Hyundai driver, Ali Waqar, 27, also sustained injuries to his right shoulder, left leg and thigh.

items.title: Ringgit holds steady against US dollar at opening
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit held steady against the US dollar at Thursday's opening as investors awaited the release of US consumer price index (CPI) data on Friday. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US CPI data would influence expectations for the United States Federal Reserve's interest rate path and could weigh on market sentiment. Mohd Afzanizam said Brent crude oil prices were hovering at US$101.21 a barrel as tensions between the United States and Iran were expected to escalate.

items.title: Tok Mat: ‘Rumah Bangsa’ should anchor Malay unity, but Umno won’t form new political alliance
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Umno is open to Malay unity at any time, but any such cooperation must be sincere, strategic and anchored by the concept of “Rumah Bangsa”, said party deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan. Mohamad, better known as Tok Mat, said Umno remained open to working with Malay parties regardless of their political ideology, provided the cooperation was based on a clear understanding of the interests and future of the Malay community. “Umno is open to Malay unity at any time.

items.title: NRD: 365 foreigners charged over fake MyKad, birth certificate offences in eight months
items.summary: PORT KLANG, Sept 10 — The National Registration Department (NRD) disclosed that 365 foreigners were charged in court over MyKad and birth certificate fraud between January and August this year. Enforcement director Mazhad Abdul Aziz said 738 joint operations were conducted with various agencies nationwide, including raids on premises and factories to detect the use of fraudulent identification documents. “Of that number, 286 cases involved the use of fake identity cards or cards belonging to others, while another 79 were linked to forged birth certificates.

items.title: Handyman charged with threatening to kill mum, burn house over RM2,500
items.summary: BATU PAHAT: A handyman was charged in the magistrate's court here today with threatening to kill his mother and burn down her house after she allegedly refused to give him RM2,500. The unmarried accused allegedly threatened to cause the death of his 50-year-old mother and destroy her house in Jalan Parit Kemang, Senggarang, at 8.40am on Sept 6. He allegedly made the threats after his mother refused his request for RM2,500.

items.title: Malayan Cement stocked up against coal supply disruptions
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malayan Cement Bhd is well-positioned to weather potential coal supply disruptions from Indonesia, having secured sufficient stocks until November, according to CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd. The YTL Group-controlled cement producer's share price has come under selling pressure since mid-August amid investor concerns over disruptions to coal supply and renewed tensions in the Middle East. CIMB Securities also expects domestic cement prices to remain fairly stable.

items.title: Man found dead with hands, feet tied inside sewage tank in Nibong Tebal
items.summary: NIBONG TEBAL, Sept 10 — Police discovered a man’s body at a house in Lorong 7, Taman Seri Bistari here today. Seberang Perai Selatan deputy police chief DSP Mohd Norazmi Abd Ghapar said the deceased’s identity is being verified and a post-mortem will be conducted to determine the cause of death. “Police are conducting further investigations.

items.title: Remains of doctor killed in Sarawak helicopter crash to be buried in Kota Bharu after forensic procedures
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Sept 10 — The remains of Dr Ainul Baraah Kamarudin, 33, one of five killed in a helicopter crash in Sarawak, are expected to be buried at the Sri Kedeper Muslim Cemetery here upon completion of forensic procedures. Her father, Kamarudin Salleh, 69, said funeral prayers for Dr Ainul would be held at Masjid Al Karamah in Mukim Baung Besar, Pengkalan Chepa. Meanwhile, Miri Division Resident Galong Luang, who is also Miri Division Disaster Management Committee chairman, confirmed that all five aboard the helicopter died in the crash at about 3.40 pm yesterday.

items.title: ‘Forever centrist’: Tok Mat insists Umno won’t veer left or right
items.summary: Mohamad, better known as Tok Mat, said Umno’s ideology was rooted in centrism and that the party would continue to take the middle ground as a national party. “My emphasis is that Umno will forever be centrist. He said Umno would not lean to the left or right, but would seek to balance ideas from both sides while remaining a moderate national party.

items.title: Mother and two sons found dead after being trapped in Kluang house fire
items.summary: The Johor Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM), in a statement, said it received an emergency call at 10.44 pm before 14 personnel from the Kluang Fire and Rescue Station (BBP) arrived at the scene about five minutes later. “The fire involved a two-storey terrace house measuring 16 feet by 70 feet, with about 50 per cent of the house’s structure engulfed in flames. The operation also involved two SITRAK fire engines and an Emergency Medical Rescue Services (EMRS) unit.

items.title: Sarikei records country's highest API reading at 194
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Sarikei recorded the highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading in the country at 194 as of 8am today, as 15 areas nationwide registered unhealthy air quality amid the ongoing transboundary haze. Checks on the Department of Environment's (DOE) Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal showed Sarawak dominating the unhealthy list, with 10 of the 15 locations in the state. Bukit Rambai in Melaka rounded out the unhealthy list at 104.

items.title: Kluang hospital faces manpower shortage as bed capacity expands
items.summary: KLUANG: A shortage of manpower is putting pressure on Enche' Besar Hajjah Kalsom Hospital here as its bed capacity and specialist services expand to meet the needs of more than 330,000 people. Johor Health and Environment Committee chairman Ling Tian Soon said the hospital currently has 396 beds, with another 38 expected to be added once Ward 10B upgrading works are completed by the end of September. "However, the hospital is now facing a shortage of manpower.

items.title: ‘Kayfa haluka?’: Warm Umno welcome for PAS delegates at assembly
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — The first PAS delegates to attend an Umno general assembly received a warm welcome from party members here last night. Umno deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan welcomed three PAS Muslimat delegates while opening the simultaneous assemblies of the party’s Wanita, Pemuda and Puteri wings. “ Umno leaders attended PAS’ annual muktamar last week, and in a reciprocal gesture, Umno secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the party had invited PAS’ top leadership to its general assembly.

items.title: Woman, two sons killed in Kluang house fire
items.summary: KLUANG: A woman and her two sons were killed in a fire at a two-storey terrace house in Taman Titiwangsa here last night. "The fire involved a two-storey terrace house measuring 16 feet by 70 feet, with about 50 per cent of the house's structure engulfed in flames. The operation involved two fire engines and an Emergency Medical Rescue Services unit.

items.title: Malaysian embassy receives Ethiopian delegation ahead of Enkutatash
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Embassy of Malaysia in Addis Ababa received a high-level Ethiopian delegation on Tuesday for a courtesy visit, reflecting the positive bilateral engagement between the two countries ahead of Enkutatash, the Ethiopian New Year. Representing the Ethiopian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Amha Hailegeorgis conveyed the Ethiopian Government's New Year greetings to the Malaysian mission. This year's celebration marks the start of the Ethiopian year 2019.

items.title: Tok Mat admits Umno’s DAP ties were hard to sell to Malay voters
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Umno has struggled to convince the majority of Malay voters to accept its cooperation with DAP in the federal Government, party deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said today. “Look at how Umno has tried to justify and explain its cooperation with DAP in the Unity Government. “There is no argument that can convince the majority of the Malay constituency, or soften their position, to accept Umno’s cooperation with DAP in the Unity Government.

items.title: Umno general assembly: Strategic recalibration, reform ambitions and the test of political renewal
items.summary: THE 2026 Umno general assembly, being held at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur from yesterday till Saturday, is expected to see more than 6,400 delegates across the main assembly and the Wanita, Pemuda and Puteri wings. Pre-assembly programmes have already addressed Islamic scholarship, Malay education, women, artificial intelligence and the digital economy. The setting combines tradition with an attempt to frame Umno's relevance around social and technological change.

items.title: When power corrupts organisations
items.summary: Power is necessary for organisations to function. Directors need authority to make strategic decisions, chief executives need power to allocate resources, and managers need sufficient authority to lead their teams. Initially, concentration of power may appear beneficial.

items.title: From construction to chips, Malaysia's data centre boom spreads
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's data centre boom is spreading deeper into the economy, creating new opportunities across construction, power infrastructure and the technology supply chain, analysts said. It is estimated that Malaysia's data centre capacity could reach eight to nine gigawatts (GW) by 2030, creating a RM128 billion to RM162 billion market for the domestic mechanical and electrical (M&E) sector. The ripple effect is also being felt elsewhere in the technology ecosystem, with company earnings tracked by RHB Research more than tripling in the second quarter on stronger factory loadings.

items.title: US blacklists Ecuador's 'Tiguerones' as terror group
items.summary: QUITO: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Wednesday designated Ecuador's Los Tiguerones gang a "terrorist organisation" during a visit to Quito, escalating Washington's campaign against criminal groups it says are destabilising Latin America. Los Tiguerones have been linked to cocaine trafficking, extortion, contract killings, arms trafficking and money laundering. Los Tiguerones is the latest Ecuadoran gang to be designated a terrorist organisation by Washington, joining Los Choneros, Los Lobos and Chone Killers.

items.title: 2027 Budget will have to impute higher crude oil price assumptions
items.summary: Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said a prudent oil price assumption for the 2027 Budget would be around US$90 a barrel, given prevailing geopolitical uncertainties in West Asia. He said the average Brent crude price stood at US$82.18 a barrel in 2023, US$79.85 in 2024 and US$68.19 in 2025, while the average price from early January to September 9 this year was US$87.59. Afzanizam said maintaining the existing fuel subsidy structure if oil prices remained around US$100 a barrel would involve a policy trade-off, with greater resources allocated to subsidies potentially requiring cuts in other areas.

items.title: IAEA board refers Iran to UN Security Council
items.summary: VIENNA: The IAEA board of governors on Wednesday voted to refer Iran to the UN Security Council over its nuclear "non-compliance" in a diplomatic move to pile pressure on the Islamic republic. The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) has not had access to key nuclear facilities in Iran since Israel, joined by the United States, launched a 12-day conflict in June 2025 that included strikes on nuclear sites. It "requests the (IAEA) director general to report" Iran to the Security Council and the General Assembly of the United Nations.

items.title: Evacuations in Malibu after waves open sinkhole at Nicolas Cage's house
items.summary: LOS ANGELES: People living in an upmarket coastal stretch of Malibu were under an evacuation order Wednesday after a giant sinkhole opened up on the driveway of a beachfront home belonging to Oscar-winning US actor Nicolas Cage. The enormous hole appeared Tuesday as heavy surf – brought by the after-effects of a hurricane – pounded the exclusive coastline, which is home to some of California's wealthiest people and a host of celebrities. Malibu city officials issued an evacuation order affecting dozens of homes in some of the most sought-after real estate in Southern California.

items.title: Gerakan treasurer quits after 31 years amid 'unease' over Pas ties [WATCH]
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Gerakan treasurer Hng Chee Wey's resignation after 31 years could signal growing unease over the party's ties with Pas within Perikatan Nasional (PN), sources say. Sources familiar with the situation said Hng's departure could signal deeper concerns within Gerakan, with one suggesting that "this may be just the beginning". Gerakan deputy president and Penang Gerakan chairman Oh Tong Keong confirmed Hng's resignation, saying the party was surprised by the decision.

items.title: Malaysia’s data centre boom: How it affects jobs, electricity and water
items.summary: Much of that happens in data centres — facilities that house computer servers and other equipment used to store, process and transmit data. Malaysia is seeing growing investment in data centres and cloud computing as demand for digital services and artificial intelligence increases. What exactly is a data centre?

items.title: Proposal to shut 4 Redang coral sites for 2 years
items.summary: THE Terengganu government has received a proposal to stop snorkelling and diving activities at four of Pulau Redang's 15 coral reef sites for two years to allow the ecosystems to recover. The Pasir Akar, Pulau Lima, Pulau Paku Besar and Pulau Ekor Tebu sites are said to have suffered more than 80 per cent coral damage. State Tourism, Culture, Environment and Climate Change Committee chairman Datuk Razali Idris said the proposal was submitted by resort operators and Reef Check Malaysia.

items.title: Persevere and you'll succeed, says veteran-turned-entrepreneur
items.summary: DECADES after fighting communist insurgents in Sarawak, army veteran Rahizad Abdullah believes that a soldier's duty does not end when he hangs up his uniform. The 64-year-old urges fellow veterans to take up new pursuits, including entrepreneurship. "Entrepreneurship is another 'struggle', just like serving in the army.

items.title: Malaysia's affluent investors embrace AI
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Affluent and high-net-worth investors in Malaysia are among the world's biggest adopters of artificial intelligence (AI) for financial and investment purposes, HSBC Bank Malaysia Bhd said. It found that 85 per cent of Malaysian respondents use AI for financial and investment purposes, placing Malaysia among the top three markets surveyed, alongside China at 85 per cent and just behind India at 86 per cent. Despite the high adoption of AI, financial professionals and institutions remain investors' leading source of investment ideas, cited by 65 per cent of respondents.

items.title: Netanyahu under fire over report he ignored UAE's Oct 7 warning
items.summary: ISRAELI opposition leaders on Tuesday called Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu unfit to serve after a bombshell report that the United Arab Emirates (UAE) had warned him before the Oct 7, 2023 Hamas attack. Netanyahu's office denied the report by the left-leaning newspaper, saying in a statement on Tuesday: "No warning was given to the prime minister from the UAE before Oct 7." "Netanyahu received dozens of warnings for Oct 7 and ignored them all.

items.title: Apple unveils RM8,134 passport-shaped foldable iPhone Duo [WATCH]
items.summary: CUPERTINO, California: Apple on Wednesday unveiled a US$1,999 (about RM8,134) foldable phone called Duo, introducing the biggest change in years in the company's flagship product. When open, it is Apple's thinnest phone, the company said. Apple said the iPhone Duo will feature the A20 chip to drive its displays and also a new C2 modem chip designed by Apple, part of its move away from Qualcomm's wireless data chips.

items.title: Sarawak channels RM100,000 to each family of helicopter crash victim
items.summary: KUCHING: The Sarawak government will channel a contribution of RM100,000 to each family of personnel involved in the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash in Long Lellang. In a statement on social media by the Sarawak Public Communications Unit (UKAS), the state government announced it will also fully cover the education fees of the victims' children who are still in school through the Sarawak Foundation. "Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg agreed that the assistance be channelled as a sign of the Sarawak State Government's concern to help ease the burden of the families and the next of kin involved.

items.title: Cyberattack ruled out in UK air traffic glitch as more flights axed
items.summary: LONDON: UK air travellers faced more misery Wednesday with 177 flights scrapped across the country, as Britain's air traffic control service scrambled to recover from a technical glitch which it ruled out as a cyberattack. Nearly all the latest flights were at London Heathrow, Britain's busiest airport, FlightRadar24 wrote on X. The head of the National Air Traffic Services (NATS), Martin Rolfe, meanwhile said "we have at this point ruled out cyber" as a cause.

items.title: Cluster bomb casualties near record, driven by war in Ukraine
items.summary: GENEVA: Cluster munitions killed or wounded at least 1,063 people in 2025 — most of them in Ukraine — in the third-highest annual toll on record, according to a report released ahead of a conference reviewing a treaty banning the weapons. The vast majority of the casualties — 87 per cent — were civilians, and around two-fifths were children, the Cluster Munition Coalition's annual report said on Tuesday. Ukraine has also used cluster munitions, the report found.

items.title: Iran says 'prohibited zone' extends beyond Hormuz into parts of Arabian Sea
items.summary: TEHERAN: Iran's Revolutionary Guards on Wednesday said a new "prohibited zone" would cover waters many kilometres beyond the Strait of Hormuz and apply to ships as far as the Arabian Sea. Iran had first announced the "prohibited zone" earlier this week as it continued talks with Oman over a temporary shipping route through the strait. On Tuesday, Iranian forces said they struck 10 vessels that attempted to cross Hormuz without coordination.

items.title: Spain records 61 heatwave days in 2026, highest on record
items.summary: MADRID: Spain recorded 61 days under heatwave conditions across the mainland and Balearic Islands in 2026, the highest number on record and far above the previous peak of 41 days in 2022, national weather agency AEMET said on Wednesday. Spain also experienced its hottest summer since records began in 1961, with an average temperature of 24.5 degrees Celsius, 0.3 degrees above the previous record set in 2025 and 2.4 degrees above the 1991-2020 average. Four heatwaves affected mainland Spain and the Balearic Islands, including a six-day episode in early September, AEMET said, meaning that Spain experienced extremely high temperatures on approximately two out of every three days of the summer.

items.title: Covenant unveils low-cost cruise missile with US$150m in orders
items.summary: WASHINGTON: Defence startup Covenant on Wednesday unveiled a heavy-payload, long-range cruise missile it says can be quickly mass-produced at a relatively low cost, in the latest challenge to major US weapons makers from some of Silicon Valley's biggest investors. The announcement from Covenant after two years of development coincides with efforts by the US and its allies to restock missile inventories with less expensive and plentiful long-range precision-strike missiles after the war in Iran depleted stocks of the critical armaments. Its missile, called Anthem, is a ground-launched cruise missile carrying a payload of more than 200kg.

items.title: Nepal turns to drones to deliver flood relief
items.summary: DEVIGHAT: With roads and bridges destroyed and helicopters busy with search and rescue operations after last month's devastating floods, Nepal's army is turning to drones to deliver relief to displaced people. "Most of our helicopters are busy with rescue operations. In addition to aid delivery, drones have also been used to move the bodies of flood victims in some affected areas, while reconnaissance drones have also been heavily used in search and rescue operations.

items.title: Imelda Marcos US$200m graft case dismissed by Philippine Supreme Court
items.summary: MANILA: The Philippine Supreme Court tossed out a graft case against former first lady Imelda Marcos that had languished in the courts for years, documents released on Wednesday show. On Wednesday, court documents revealed the Supreme Court dismissed the case more than two months ago. The case is not the first against Imelda Marcos to be overturned by the Supreme Court.

items.title: UK police expand donations probe into Farage's Reform party
items.summary: LONDON: British police said Wednesday they had widened a criminal investigation into allegations that Nigel Farage's hard-right Reform UK party accepted illegal donations following new claims last week. The announcement increases pressure on Farage, who has endured months of intense scrutiny over Reform's financial arrangements which has coincided with the party losing its lead in opinion polls. Farage and his hard-right, anti-immigration party deny any impropriety.

items.title: Umno president urges party to strengthen solidarity, machinery
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Strengthening solidarity, streamlining party machinery and staying close to the people were among the key messages delivered by Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi at a briefing today, as the party gears up for the next election. Umno vice-president Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said Ahmad Zahid urged party members to be grateful for the victories in the Johor and Negeri Sembilan state elections, and not to become complacent. Another vice-president, Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, said Ahmad Zahid reminded party members not to become arrogant following Barisan Nasional’s (BN) victories in the two state elections.

items.title: Zahid denies N. Sembilan MB resigned amid royal dispute
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has denied claims that Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim has submitted his resignation amid a dispute involving the state’s royal institution. Ahmad Zahid also denied being present at an alleged meeting where Ismail was purportedly made to sign a proclamation seeking the removal of Negri Sembilan Ruler Tuanku Muhriz Munawir. Ismail himself has denied this,” he said.

items.title: Zara Qairina inquest: Mother’s assessment unnecessary for psychological autopsy, psychiatrist tells court
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 9 — Consultant Forensic Psychiatrist Dr Chua Sze Hung told the Coroner’s Court today that an assessment of the mother of the late Zara Qairina Mahathir was not necessary in the context and framework of a psychological autopsy. Dr Chua, who was recalled to testify, explained that an assessment of the surviving parent was not a proper clinical or methodological substitute for a retrospective assessment of the deceased adolescent’s mental state. Meanwhile, Dr Chua said clinical psychiatric assessment is not meant to be done retrospectively or to answer the manner of death.

items.title: Anwar remembers Capt Zainol Afiq as kind man, pays tribute to pilot’s service (VIDEO)
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim remembers Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, the pilot who was killed in yesterday’s helicopter crash in Sarawak, as a kind man of good character. He said the pilot’s service and contributions would always be remembered, and urged his family to inform his staff if they needed any assistance. The prime minister said he would also contact the families of the other victims killed in the crash.

items.title: Finance Ministry: Unsubsidised petrol, diesel prices rise 25 sen per litre from tomorrow
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — The retail prices of RON97 petrol, unsubsidised RON95 petrol and unsubsidised diesel will each increase by 25 sen per litre for the period from September 10 to 16, 2026. MOF said diesel prices in the international market also rose faster than crude oil prices due to constraints on refining capacity and declining inventories. If this situation persists, declining inventories and increasingly tight supplies of refined petroleum products could increase risk premiums on global petrol and diesel prices,” MOF said.

items.title: Former Felda subsidiary CEO gets four-day remand extension in corruption probe
items.summary: A source said the remand order, which runs from tomorrow until September 13, was issued by Magistrate Ezrene Zakaria after the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) made the application at the Putrajaya Magistrate’s Court here this morning. “The remand application was made after the suspect’s initial remand period ended today. The suspect was previously remanded for three days from last Monday,” the source said.

items.title: Anwar: PM’s Cup debate nurtures confident, critical young minds
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — The Prime Minister’s Cup Debate Competition is more than a platform for testing debating skills, serving an important role in developing young people who are confident in speaking up, think critically, and respect differing views, Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. In a Facebook post, the prime minister said the competition continues the legacy of Tun Abdul Razak Hussein by providing young people with a platform to test their courage, deepen their knowledge and sharpen their debating skills. The Prime Minister’s Cup Debate Competition was first held in 1974 at the Malay College Kuala Kangsar in Perak.

items.title: Azalina, Asyraf Wajdi deny attending meeting linked to alleged bid to remove Tuanku Muhriz
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Two Umno leaders have denied attending a meeting allegedly linked to claims that Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim had signed a declaration seeking to remove Tuanku Muhriz Munawir as the state’s Yang di-Pertuan Besar. The denials came from Umno secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dasuki and Umno information chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said, Harian Metro reported today. Azalina said she was unaware of the alleged matter.

items.title: Alam Maritim Resources CEO Azmi Ahmad to be charged over Tabung Haji probe
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Alam Maritim Resources Bhd group managing director and chief executive officer (CEO) Datuk Azmi Ahmad will be charged at the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court tomorrow. Based on a check of the court system, Azmi will be charged at Criminal Sessions Court 14 before Judge Suzana Hussin at 9am. On August 15, Bernama reported that MACC had detained seven individuals comprising a CEO, a company director, a former company director and four former senior management officers of Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) to assist in investigations into issues raised in the Royal Commission of Inquiry Report on Tabung Haji.

items.title: Hubline confirms helicopter in fatal Long Lellang crash was operated by subsidiary
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Shipping and aviation services company Hubline Bhd has confirmed that the helicopter involved in the accident at the Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing Airport (STOLport) in Sarawak on Tuesday was operated by its unit, Layang Layang Aerospace Sdn Bhd (LLA). In a filing with Bursa Malaysia today, Hubline said the helicopter, bearing registration number 9M-LLF, was conducting a flying doctor service (FDS) flight when the accident occurred. “The helicopter was operating a FDS flight with five persons on board, including the pilot,” it said.

items.title: Remains of five Long Lellang helicopter crash victims recovered, DNA identification to follow
items.summary: MIRI, Sept 9 — The five victims in the helicopter which crashed in Long Lellang on Tuesday have been recovered, said Sarawak Police Commissioner Datuk Mohamad Zainal Abdullah. Mohamad Zainal said formal identification would be carried out at Miri Hospital, where the remains and tissue samples would also be sent for further examination and DNA testing. Sarawak Police Commissioner Datuk Mohamad Zainal Abdullah said formal identification would be carried out at Miri Hospital, where the remains and tissue samples would also be sent for further examination and DNA testing.

items.title: Umno delegates enter assembly on an election high after Johor, N. Sembilan wins, with Melaka next on the radar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Umno delegates arrived for the first day of the party’s annual assembly today in an upbeat mood following its back-to-back victories in Johor and Negeri Sembilan, with Melaka now emerging as the next electoral target. Umno Youth Damansara committee member Muhammad Najeeh Norazam, 33, said the two state election victories had given delegates a morale boost and changed the atmosphere within the party. Umno Youth Damansara committee member Muhammad Najeeh Norazam, 33, said the two state election victories had given delegates a morale boost and changed the atmosphere within the party.

items.title: RM1.25b solar hybrid project corruption case: Prosecution challenges ruling allowing Rosmah to adduce additional evidence
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 9 — The prosecution has filed an application to stay the Court of Appeal’s decision that granted Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor leave to adduce additional evidence in her appeal against her conviction in the RM1.25 billion solar hybrid project corruption case. The application for stay seeks to temporarily suspend the taking of additional evidence pending the disposal of the prosecution’s appeal before the Federal Court. On August 1, a three-member Court of Appeal bench comprising Justices Datuk Azhahari Kamal Ramli, Datuk Dr Choo Kah Sing, and K. Muniandy allowed Rosmah’s application to adduce additional evidence.

items.title: Former Tabung Haji chairman, CEO among five held over hibah, AMLA probes
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Police have detained five people, including a former Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) chairman and former chief executive officer (CEO), to assist investigations into matters involving the pilgrimage fund. The five suspects comprise three men and two women aged between 48 and 70, including a former TH chairman, former CEO, former chief financial officer and serving TH personnel. Rusdi said investigations were ongoing.

items.title: Haze: Serian records API 213, highest air pollution level in Sarawak
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Serian in Sarawak continued to record a very unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) reading due to haze this afternoon. Eight other areas in Sarawak recorded unhealthy API readings, namely Samarahan (186), Kuching (183), Sarikei (174), Miri Industrial Training Institute (166), Samalaju (165), Sri Aman (159), Bintulu (157) and Mukah (151). An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 (moderate), 101 to 200 (unhealthy), 201 to 300 (very unhealthy) and 300 and above as hazardous.

items.title: Dengue cases soar 66pc, deaths hit 62 in Malaysia, almost double 2025 toll
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Dengue fever cases nationwide have increased sharply by 66 per cent with 65,979 infections recorded as of Epidemiological Week 35 compared with 39,616 during the same period last year, says Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. The unity government spokesman said the issue was among those discussed at the Cabinet meeting today, with the number of deaths due to dengue also showing a significant increase. He said 62 cases of deaths due to dengue were recorded up to the 35th epidemiological week of this year, compared to 32 cases in the same period last year.

items.title: Umno says Pakatan applying double standard on royal pardons, points to Anwar’s 2018 case
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Umno today accused Pakatan Harapan (PH) of applying a double standard on royal pardons after the coalition said those convicted in high-profile corruption cases should serve their full sentences. Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said PH had supported the full pardon granted to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim in 2018 even though he had not completed his five-year prison term at the time. he said in a statement uploaded on Facebook.

items.title: Fahmi: Malaysia ready to help Indonesia fight forest fires, awaiting green light
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Malaysia is on standby and prepared to assist Indonesia in managing the forest fires that have caused haze in the region, government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today. “For us to deploy our assets to assist, we need the permission by the Indonesian authorities,” said Fahmi, who is also the communications minister. Yesterday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim called for improvements to the existing Asean mechanism for tackling transboundary haze to ensure such incidents could be addressed effectively.

items.title: MACC: Abdul Azeez chose to remain in purple lock-up attire, handcuffs for court appearance
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Former Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim chose to wear purple police lock-up attire and handcuffs when he appeared in the Sessions Court here today, the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) said. In a statement, the MACC said its officers, the police escorting Abdul Azeez and his lawyer had advised him to change into ordinary clothes before he was taken to court. However, the MACC said Abdul Azeez insisted on remaining in the lock-up attire and handcuffs until the charge against him had been read.

items.title: Cabinet expresses condolences to families of five killed in Sarawak FDS helicopter crash
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — The Cabinet today expressed its condolences to the families of the five victims who died in the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Ulu Baram, Sarawak, yesterday. Unity government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and all ministers offered their sympathies and condolences at the weekly Cabinet meeting today. Fahmi, who is also the communications minister, said Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad had earlier announced the identities of all five victims.

items.title: Malaysian woman held at Delhi airport with 15kg cannabis worth RM2.2m
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — A Malaysian woman was arrested by Indian authorities after she was caught attempting to smuggle 15 kilogrammes of cannabis, valued at approximately 52.5 million rupees (RM2.2 million), at Indira Gandhi International Airport on Sept 4. Delhi Customs (Airport & General) in a statement on X said the passenger, who arrived from Kuala Lumpur on flight OD-205, was intercepted at Terminal 3 based on profile-based targeting. An examination of her trolley bag led to the discovery of 30 polythene pouches containing suspected ganja (cannabis) weighing 15,015.5 grammes (net weight)," the department said.
